intuition: Typed letters define a prefix. A trie follows that prefix without scanning every sentence. At each prefix node, save the three best matching sentences. When '#' finishes a sentence, increase its count and refresh the affected saved suggestions. Start a new prefix after that marker.

A committed sentence is the only sentence whose frequency changes. For a node on its path, the new leaders must come from the previous leaders plus that changed sentence: every other outsider keeps the same rank relative to the old leaders. Sorting this at-most-four-item candidate list restores the correct cache.

The object also remembers the current prefix and its trie node between calls. A missing edge means no historical sentence matches the current query; it remains missing until the query ends. On #, insert the completed sentence, update its prefix caches, and reset the cursor to the root for a new query.

steps: Initialize history with i love you:5, island:3, ironman:2, and i love leetcode:2. The i-prefix cache retains the top three.
Input i moves to that prefix node and returns [i love you,island,i love leetcode]. The space in i love leetcode sorts before ironman’s r when counts tie.
Input space extends the query to i . Its cache returns [i love you,i love leetcode]; island no longer matches.
Input a extends the query to i a. No matching child exists, so the current node becomes absent and the result is [].
Input # adds the completed sentence i a with count 1 and refreshes caches along its character path.
Reset prefix to the empty string and node to the root, then return []. The stored new sentence can participate in subsequent queries.

codeNotes.note: Only existing leaders and the updated sentence can become the new leaders; copying permits safe local reranking.
Negated counts sort hottest first; the second key breaks ties by ascending sentence text, including spaces.
A commit ends the old query. Resetting the trie cursor is necessary even when its previous prefix had no matches.

keyDecision: Rank by larger usage count first, then smaller character order for ties. '#' records the sentence and returns no suggestions.
